A1.justification: Both complete, readable 24-page PDFs describe the same robotic-hand co-design work, retitled with 'House of Dextra' in v3. Text and rendered-page comparison cover the equations, tables, figures, and appendices; the appendices are unchanged.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulation experiments, physical-hand deployment results, controller comparisons, and morphology sensitivity analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including simulation comparisons, rotation tests on 17 unseen real objects, and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: The graph-grammar generator, morphology-conditioned policy, design search, and blind deployment remain. The revised transfer paragraph removes checkpoint-adaptation detail without establishing an actual change to the procedure; fine-tuning remains described elsewhere.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same rotation, grasping, and flipping tasks, simulated object collection, and 17 unseen real objects. The appendix controller tests and LEAP morphology-analysis coverage also remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same RoboGrammar, Monte Carlo, MPPI, LEAP, and fine-tuning comparisons. Appendix 9.1 retains the MPPI/Cross Entropy Method tests and individually trained PPO comparator; v3's new cross-reference adds no comparator.

E3.justification: The reported search budget of 50 iterations with 40 designs each, 128 randomized environments per design, evaluation procedures, and Tables 4–5 randomization settings are unchanged. Appendix 9.1.2 retains the same 1,000-versus-350-epoch comparison protocol.

E4.justification: The controller-failure tests, cross-embodied versus individual PPO analysis, fine-tuning comparison, and morphology sensitivity analyses are retained. The added Section 5.1 reference highlights an analysis already present in Appendix 9.1.2.

E5.justification: Statistical summaries and displays, including task variability and parameter correlations, are unchanged. Neither version adds or removes seed information, repeated-run reporting, confidence intervals, or significance testing relative to the other.

E6.justification: Numerical results and plotted findings match, including Table 1's 3.3 and 1.85 rad/s results with and without fine-tuning and all Table 3 entries. The new sentence about benefits over individual PPO restates findings already reported in v1's Appendix 9.1.2.

T1.justification: The graph and MDP definitions, bi-level optimization formulation, and design and policy objectives are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and concluding lessons retain the same contributions concerning scalable co-design, manufacturable hands, task-specific morphology, and deployment within 24 hours. The new title introduces branding without changing these claims.

C2.justification: Section 5.1 newly summarizes the policy-generalization interpretation already present in Appendix 9.1.2. Explanations of morphology effects, failure conditions, applicability, and the Section 8 limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 3.2 removes the explicit statement that the family-policy checkpoint is loaded and its weights fine-tuned for observations without object state. The title-page project address also changes, while the introduction retains the previous address; the PDFs do not establish any change in online availability.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and bibliography are unchanged. The relationships to prior co-design, cross-embodiment learning, and sim-to-real research remain the same.

P1.justification: v3 adds 'House of Dextra' to the title, locally rewrites and splits the transfer paragraph, and adds an appendix cross-reference in Section 5.1. Section ordering and the broader narrative structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 1's caption adds the framework name, and Figure 2's caption replaces 'fine tuned control' with 'control pairs.' Small spacing and layout adjustments occur, including around Table 3; figure panels, plots, and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: The added Appendix 9.1.2 pointer improves navigation, but Section 3.2 loses the explicit explanation of adapting the family-policy checkpoint to blind observations. This makes the simulation-to-deployment transition slightly less clear and reproducible. The otherwise unchanged scientific content and limited presentation edits do not compensate for that documentation loss.
